records.title: #378373 - The Society for the Exploration of EurAsia
records.description: Swiss research institute that funds Central Asian archeological excavations (Sogdian, etc.), with online pages for their excavation reports. Gesellschaft zur Erforschung EurAsiens " The aim of the Society for the Exploration of EurAsia is to make a scientific contribution to the exploration of the cultures of Eurasia. It promotes the scientific exchange of ideas and experience and supports fieldwork in the fields of archaeology, history of art and history of religions. It will conduct its fieldwork in close cooperation with local scientists and institutions outside the political boundaries of the European Union. For this purpose, the Society cooperates with academics, interested parties, potential sponsors, institutions and authorities at national and international levels. The Society requires that all findings remain in the respective countries and may be only exported short-term for the purposes of restoration, analysis and temporary exhibitions based on the consent by the local authorities. ... The Society supports projects whose fieldwork takes place within Eurasia and outside the political boundaries of the European Union. The projects must be carried out in cooperation with the local experts and institutions. The key focus of the projects lies on the scientific fieldwork; the Society does not support projects which only serve for reconnoitering or private travel purposes. " https://www.exploration-eurasia.com/index.htm

records.title: #327058 - Khwarazm AR tetradrachm, Unnamed King A.
records.description: Ex The New York Sale Auction 60 9-10 Jan 2024 lot 201. Estimate: 100 000 USD Khwarazmia. Unnamed King A. Silver Tetradrachm (15.49 g), mid-late 1st century BC. Bearded bust right with a roundish face and large nose, wearing a cap-like kulah headdress with a posterior flap, a narrow diadem with a zigzag pattern, straight-lined ties going down back, and a pellet-in-annulet ornament; behind, Nike flying crowning him with a wreath; all within a bead-a-reel border. Reverse: IYIYEΩIE ΠΓAVI.H, EIYΛYIΛY below, king on horseback right; behind, "swan-shaped" tamgha . Fedorov, "Notes on the numismatics of ancient Khwarezm," Revue Numismatique 2005, p.166, 2. Excessively rare - we found no record of another specimen of this type ever sold. Deep slate-gray tone. Extremely Fine. Price realized: 130 000 USD

records.title: #16558 - Khwarezm, AR tetradrachm, unknown ruler (Vainberg AIII), ca 1st century AD
records.description: CNG, Inc., Triton VIII, Jan 10, 2005; Lot 667 : ANCIENT. KINGS of KHWARAZMIA. Artav (Artabanos). Circa 1st-2nd century AD. AR Tetradrachm (13.29 gm, 1h). Bearded bust right, wearing cap-like headdress with posterior flap; behind, Nike flying right, crowning king with laurel wreath held in his right hand / IUIUEWIE MELUI EILUILU (blundered Greek legend), king on horseback right; tamgha behind. B.I. Vainberg, Monety drevnego Khorezma (Moscow, 1977), pg. 109, 7 = CAAU 307; S.P. Tolstov, "The Coins of the Shahs of Ancient Khwarizm and the Ancient Khwarizmi Alphabet," Vestnik drevney Istorii (Moscow, 1938), pl. VI, 1 = R.B. Whitehead, " Notes on the Indo-Greeks, Part II," NumChron 1947, pg. 38, fig. 3 = Göbl, Dokumente, pl. V = MIG Type 498. VF, light scratches in reverse field. Extremely rare, the third known specimen. Coins of the kingdom of Khwarazmia from the ancient era are extremely rare, and consist of only a handful of examples. The coinage begins with barbarous imitations of tetradrachms of Eukratides I of Baktria, but in the last century BC, the Khwarazmians develop their own types, assimilating characteristics of Baktrian, Parthian, and Indo-Skythian prototypes. On the coins of this king, the Eukratides/Heraios prototype tetradrachm has a bust similar to the Parthian style with Nike crowning the king, and a Skythian-like tamgha on the reverse that serves as a symbol of all Khwarazmian coins until their demise in the 8th or 9th century AD. The bust also has purely native characteristics, such as the cap-like headdress. Truly a wonderful example of the ancient coinage of central Asia. Estimate $5000 / Sold For $6250. This amount does not include the buyer’s fee.

records.title: #141162 - Khwarezm, AR tetradrachm, unknown ruler (Vainberg AIII), ca 1st century AD
records.description: Paul-Francis Jacquier Numismatique Antique, Auction 39, 12 September 2014; Lot 211 : CHORESMIEN Artav (Artabanos), 1. Jh. n. Chr. Tetradrachmon. Bärtige Büste mit Diadem, Helm mit Nackenschutz und reich verziertem Panzer rechts, von Nike bekränzt, das Ganze in Perl- und Spindelkreis. Rv/ Abstrahierte griechische Leg. IYIVEWIE MELYV / EILVILV. König mit Speer n. rechts reitend; im Feld links Tamga. M. Federov, “Money Circulation of Khwarezm in the Ancient Period,” ONS Newsletter 182 (Winter 2005), S. 18. Vainberg, Gruppe A III, 7 = CAAU 307. S.P. Tolstov, "The Coins of the Shahs of Ancient Khwarizm and the Ancient Khwarizmi Alphabet," Vestnik drevney Istorii (Moscow, 1938), Taf. VI, 1 = R.B. Whitehead, "Notes on the Indo-Greeks, Part II," NC 1947, S. 38, Fig. 3 = Göbl, Dokumente, Taf. V = MIG Typ 498. Sunrise 517. 13,80 g. Äußerst selten. Gutes sehr schön Aus Auktion Triton XII (2009), 415 . Die Münzprägung von Choresmien zeigt eine Vielzahl von Typen, die in der zentralen asiatischen Region im Umlauf waren und meist auf Vorbilder aus Parthien und Baktrien zurückgreifen. Das extrem seltene Tetradrachmon von Artav – es sind nur eine handvoll Exemplare bekannt – zeigt auf dem Avers eine von Nike gekrönte Büste und erinnert an parthische Prägungen des ersten Jahrhunderts v. Chr., während das Revers einen König zu Pferde zeigt, in der Weise der späten baktrischen bzw. indo-skythischen Ausgaben. Estimate: 7'500 EUR / Starting price: 6'750 EUR / Unsold

records.title: #46087 - Khwaresmian AR coin, unidentified.
records.description: Very interesting and mysterious AR coin. As I can judge, unlisted and unique. After some investigation I couldn't identificate this coin yet. Iconography of the ruler on obverse can point both to Bivarsar as well as to Ramik. The reverse also can show last two letters the same with in Ramik's name, as well as visible two lines upon rider's head can also be corrupted Greek legends on coins earlier than Ramik's ones. However, if the coin belongs to latter one, it should be his new type, intermediate between earlier rulers' issues and common Ramik's type. For the moment I preferred to leave the coin "as is", in it's natural condition, but seriously thinking over the possibility of washing it, which can help to say firmer about it's period. I thank everyone for advance for ANY comments which are highly welcomed.

records.title: #354075 - Khwarazm AR tetradrachm, Wazamar.
records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 33 15-17 Mar 2025, lot 1622. Starting price: 250 CHF KHWARAZMIA. King Wazamar, circa 250-300. Tetradrachm (Silver, 30 mm, 8.91 g, 12 h). Within a bead-and-reel border, draped bust of Wazamar to right, with plaited hair, wearing a crown with eagle's head. Rev. King on horseback to right; Khwarazmian tamgha to left; distorted and illegible Greek legend at the sides and above; below, 'wzmʾr MLKʾ' ('King Wazamar' in Khwarazmian). Vainberg Type Б2 V. Extremely rare. Struck from slightly worn dies and the obverse somewhat rough, otherwise, very fine. The first silver coins of Khwarazmia were struck around the end of the 2nd century BC. These coins followed the types of the tetradrachms of the Greco-Bactrian king Eukratides I (circa 171–145 BC), with the tamgha (i.e., tribal mark) of the ruler added on the reverse. Around the beginning of the 2nd century AD, the depiction of the Dioscuri on the reverse was replaced with an image of the king on horseback, moving to the right. Wazamar was the last local ruler of Khwarazmia before the establishment of the Afrighid dynasty around AD 305. Since little is known about the political history of Khwarazmia before the Afrighid dynasty, the coins of the local rulers represent an extremely important source of historical information. In this regard, the coins of the Khwarazmian kings also resemble those of their Greco-Bactrian and Indo-Greek predecessors north and south of the Hindu Kush, many of whom are known to us only through their coins. Price realized: 1600 CHF

records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 33 15-17 Mar 2025, lot 1629. Starting price: 75 CHF KHWARAZMIA. King Tutukhas, 6th century. Drachm (Silver, 28 mm, 4.74 g, 1 h). Within a bead-and-reel border, draped bust of Tutukhas to right, wearing Khwarazmian head-dress decorated with a crescent and three pellets. Rev. records.title: #354076 - Khwarazm AR reduced tetradrachm, King Tutukhas.
records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 33 15-17 Mar 2025, lot 1627. Starting price: 75 CHF KHWARAZMIA. King Tutukhas, 6th century. Drachm (Silver, 29 mm, 4.84 g, 12 h). Within a bead-and-reel border, draped bust of Tutukhas to right, wearing Khwarazmian head-dress decorated with a crescent and three pellets. Rev. King on horseback to right; Khwarazmian tamgha to left; around, 'twtwhs MLKʾ' ('King Tutukhas' in Khwarazmian). Vainberg Type BI. Extremely rare. Struck from somwhat worn dies and with some scratches, otherwise, good fine. Price realized: 500 CHF

records.title: #76306 - Khwarezm, AR reduced tetradrachm, king Ramik, cut to 3.2 grams
records.description: This coin has been cut to the same weight as Zeno #41810. That one was trimmed neatly around the edges leaving a circular coin. This one was subjected to a single straight crude cut. The end result is essentially the same weight. These may be a half-denomination as suggested in the description of Zeno #41810. However, I think it is more likely that these were cut down to circulate as equals with later lighter weight coins.

records.title: #19842 - Ancient Khwaresm, King Azkatswar "Chegan".
records.description: Azkatswar "Chegan", early 8th century AD (died in 712 AD). He had been swept away by popular uprising inspired his traitorous policy of collaboration with Arab invaders. It is proposed that his lakab "Chegan" had occured from his foreign, probably Chaganian origin. That proposal could also be confirmed by reverse side of his coins. In contrast to all other Afrigid dynasty kings' coins his tamgha which resembles in appearance Chaganian one is depicted on it. Silver coins of that king are still unknown.

Sahl, ca. 809-812,Very Fine toned, RRR. VERY RARE TYPE WITH ARABIC WORD FADL BACK OF HORSE . Abu l-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Sahl ibn Zadhanfarukh al-Sarakhsi (Arabic: أبو العباس الفضل بن سهل بن زادانفروخ السرخسي‎; Abu ’l-ʿAbbās al-Faḍl b. Sahl b. Zādānfarrūḫ as-Saraḫsī, died 818), titled Dhu 'l-Ri'āsatayn ("the man of the two commands"), was a famous Persian vizier of the Abbasid era in Khurasan, who served under Caliph al-Ma'mun (r. 813–832). He played a crucial role in the civil war between al-Ma'mun and his brother al-Amin (r. 809–813), and was the de facto ruler of the Caliphate until 817.

records.title: #131268 - Khwarazm, AR reduced TDr, Azkaswar II + Dhu’l-Riyasatayn lillah.
records.description: Ex Morton & Eden LTD : Auk 66, lot 468. *Arab-Bukharan, temp. Azkaswar II (fl. 153-180h), hemidrachm, bust right, rev., horseman riding right, Dhu’l-Riyasatayn lillah in Arabic to left, 1.68g (Rtveladze 49; cf Artuk 21), good fine and rare. Dhu’l-Riyasatayn was the title of al-Fadl b. Sahl, vizier under al-Mamun (died 202h). Azkaswar II’s dates are not known for certain, but this seems likely to have been a posthumous issue struck by al-Fadl b. Sahl some years after Azkaswar himself had died.

records.title: #16559 - Khwárizm, Azkaswar II - `Abd Alláh w/Dhú-l-riyásatayn or al-Fadl
records.description: Ex CNG, Inc. : Sale: CNG 63, Lot: 915. Closing Date: May 21, 2003. KHWARAZMIAN KINGS. Sawshafan. Mid 8th Century AD. AR Drachm (2.05 gm). Estimate $400 Sold For $700 KHWARAZMIAN KINGS. Sawshafan. Mid 8th Century AD. AR Drachm (2.05 gm). Crowned head of King right / King on horseback right, holding bow. Rtveladze 49, Zeimal pg. 262, 6. Near VF, encrustation. ($400) Many areas in central Asia used Sasanian or Sasanian-style drachms for their currency. The Khwarazmians instead used drachms of their own design which portray the king wearing a turban-like crown on the obverse and the 'Khwarazmian Horseman' on the reverse. REMARK : There is a two-line arabic legend behind the rider, " Dhú-l... ". Coins are known with title Dhú-l-yaminayn, i.e. Táhir b. al-Husayn (cf. ZENO # 20661 ); or ”Dhú-l-riyásatayn”, which refers to al-Ma'mún's wazír al-Fadl bin Sahl, who was murdered/executed in 202 AH. (cf. coin with name of al-Fadl # 23805 ). Metrologically are Khwarizmian coins with Arabic names equal/close to half of Sasanian drahm or dirham tabarí.

records.title: #354080 - Syr Darya Oghuz (Ghuzz) State. AR reduced tetradrachm, ʿAbd Allah ibn Tahir.
records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 33 15-17 Mar 2025, lot 1636. Starting price: 50 CHF KHWARAZMIA. Syr Darya Oghuz (Ghuzz) State. Anonymous, 9th century. Drachm (Silver, 23 mm, 1.08 g, 7 h), citing the Tahirid ruler ʿAbd Allah ibn Tahir (AH 213-230 / AD 828-845). Afrighid-style draped bust to right with a large beaded necklace, wearing Khwarazmian royal head-dress; before head,'ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir' ('ʿAbd Allah son of Tahir' in Arabic). Rev. King on horseback to right, holding whip in his left hand; above the horse's rump, citing governor 'ʿAbd Allāh' (in Arabic). Apparently unpublished, but cf. Goncharov and Nastich Group I, variant 1 and Zeno-184343 ( for issue with governor 'Muḥammad' on the reverse). Tiny hole and some scratches, otherwise, good fine. From the inventory of an American coin dealer. Price realized: 280 CHF

records.title: #341411 - Samarqand AR hemidrachm, Antiochos-imitation.
records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 31 7-8 Sep 2024, lot 776. Starting price: 50 CHF EARLY SKYTHIANS, Uncertain. 3rd-mid 2nd century BC. Hemidrachm (Silver, 16 mm, 2.47 g, 1 h). Diademed head of Antiochos I to right. Rev. Head of a horse with reins to right within shallow incuse. Mitchiner, Ancient & Classical World, 352 var. (with symbol beneath the head of the horse). Morton & Eden 59 (2012), 789 var. (with imitative legend). Very rare and nicely toned. Struck from a worn obverse die and with some minor nicks, otherwise, very fine. From the L.I.M.B. Collection, formed over the past two decades. This type imitates the drachms of Antiochos I from Ai Khanoum (SC 431f). As viceroy of the Upper Satrapies, Antiochos I was responsible for the Seleukid East under his father. He was the driving force behind the second Hellenistic urbanization of Baktria, after a significant portion of the first generation of settlers, established under Alexander, revolted shortly after the king's death and were destroyed by Perdikkas. Although Seleukid control over Baktria could not be secured in the long term, Antiochos' efforts laid the foundation for Hellenistic Baktria, and his coins continued to circulate for a long time in and around the Baktrian heartland and in Sogdiana. Thus, it is not surprising that his horse-head drachms were imitated by local tribes. Price realized: 130 CHF

records.title: #387806 - Samarqand Soghd, AR “Samarqand Archer”, Series 2, late variant
records.description: Sogdiana, Samarqand. “Samarqand Archer” coinage, Series 2, late variant, probably struck in the third quarter of the 3rd century CE (ca. 250–275 CE). Obv.: Stylized bust of a ruler left; Sogdian legend around: xwr prnč or xwβ prnč. Rev.: Standing archer holding a bow; quiver behind the shoulder. AR; 1.49 g; 16.5 mm. Reference: A. Naymark, “Самаркандский чекан второй половины III – начала VI вв. / Samarqand coinage in the second half of the 3rd to the early 6th centuries CE,” 2020. https://www.academia.edu/44739191/

records.description: Ex Heritage World Coin Auctions NYINC Signature Sale 3122 21-22 Jan 2025, lot 34127. Starting price: 1 USD BACTRIAN KINGDOM. Euthydemus I (ca. 225-200 BC). AR tetradrachm (29mm, 16.71 gm, 12h). NGC Choice VF 5/5 - 3/5, brushed. Contemporary imitation. Attic standard. Diademed head of Euthydemus right, with soft, idealized features / BAΣIΛEΩΣ / ΕΥΘΥΔΗΜΟΥ, Heracles seated left on rock, nude, right hand balancing club on knee, leaning back on left hand; KP monogram in inner right field. Cf. Bopearachchi 9A for prototype. A fascinating example with clear and unique device styles. From the Tamco Collection. www.HA.com/TexasAuctioneerLicenseNotice Price realized: 2600 USD

records.title: #25552 - Bukhara, AR tetradrachm, Euthydemos-imitation?
records.description: Euthydemos, tetradrachm, 12,40 g. This coin looks like an ordinary Euthydemos-tetradrachm, althou a bit corroded, but that could hardly explain the low weight. Bopearachchi, in an article: "The Euthydemus imitations and the Date of the Sogdian Independence" (Silk Road Art and Archaeology) writes: ...The main criterion which enables us to identify the first imitations, whose workmanship is still very respectable compared to that of later issues, is the lighter weight of 12 g...". Mitchiner thinks such "persic weight" tetradrachms was struck in Bactria, for circulation in Sogdiana.

records.title: #282276 - Bukhara AR tetradrachm, imitating Euthydemos I.
records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Auction 10 24 Oct 2021, lot 2266. Estimate: 500 CHF LOCAL ISSUES, Sogdiana. Bukhara. Late 2nd to 1st centuries BC. Tetradrachm (Silver, 27 mm, 8.86 g, 11 h), imitating Euthydemos I of Baktria (225-220 BC). Diademed head of Euthydemos I to right. Rev. [B]AΣIΛ[EΩ]Σ - 𐡌𐡋𐡊 𐡊𐡁 (?) ('mlk' kb' in Aramaic) Herakles seated left on rock, placing his right hand on club set his on right leg and leaning left on rocky seat. Alram 1220. HGC 12, 500. MIG 481. Senior A18.3T. Very rare. A lightly toned example of expressive style. Light scratches on the obverse, otherwise, good very fine. This very interesting issue duplicates the Greek title BAΣΙΛΕΩΣ, 'king', by the Aramaic 'mlk''. Unfortunately, the reading of the rest of the legend is unclear and we do not know if 'kb' (?) was the name of a local ruler or if it had a different meaning. Price realized: 1300 CHF

records.title: #12961 - Sogdiana, king Hasa
records.description: Sogdian coin (Euthydemos-imitation) of king Hasa (according to Mitchiner, Alram has different opinion about the legend). MIG 483. Portrait - Hercules seated with club resting on knee. Aramaic legend to left, corrupt greek legend to right. Somewhere around 200 BC Euthydemos lost control of his northern possessions (Sogdiana), where a line of kings (of Kang Chu origin?) was established. This independent sogdian kingdom was overrun by scythians and YüehChi about 140-130 BC.

records.title: #282277 - Bukhara AR tetradrachm, imitating Euthydemos I, parthian-style.
records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Auction 10 24 Oct 2021, lot 2267. Estimate: 500 CHF LOCAL ISSUES, Sogdiana. Bukhara. Circa 2nd to 4th centuries AD. Tetradrachm (Silver, 27 mm, 9.71 g, 1 h), imitating Euthydemos I of Baktria (225-220 BC). Parthian-style head of a king to right, wearing diademed and radiate headdress with long locks. Rev. 'mlk' y...' (in blundered Aramaic) Deformed figure of Herakles seated left on trapezoid seat decorated with three pellets, holding club set on his right knee in his right hand and leaning left on seat. Alram 1228. HGC 12, p. 189 var. (shape of seat). MIG 494. Senior A18.5T (shape of seat). Rare. A beautifully toned and unusually attractive example. Good very fine. Ultimately also derived from Euthydemos' seated Herakles type, the appearance of a Parthian style portrait on the obverse of this issue indicates a struck date for this issue much later than is commonly assumed. It is evidence for the long-lasting influence of Greco-Baktrian coinage and culture in Central Asia long after the fall of the kingdom in circa 130 BC. Price realized: 2200 CHF

'mlk' y...' Alram 1229. HGC 12, p. 189 (shape of seat). MIG 494. Senior A18.5T (shape of seat). Rare and unusually well preserved. records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 28 9-14 Dec 2023, lot 1982. Starting price: 100 CHF LOCAL ISSUES, Sogdiana. Bukhara. Late 2nd to 1st centuries BC. Tetradrachm (Silver, 29 mm, 9.00 g, 12 h), imitating Euthydemos I of Baktria (225-220 BC), imitating the types of Euthydemos I. Parthian-style head of a king to right, wearing diademed and radiate headdress with long locks. Rev. 'mlk' y...' (in blundered Aramaic) Deformed figure of Herakles seated left on square seat decorated with three pellets, holding club set on his right knee in his right hand and leaning left on seat. Alram 1228. HGC 12, p. 189. MIG 494. Senior A18.5T. Beautifully toned and unusually attractive for the issue. A few light marks, otherwise, about extremely fine. From the collection of François Righetti, ex Jacquier 39, 12 September 2014, 209. Price realized: 2600 CHF

records.title: #17990 - Bukhara AR drahm, Great King Khunak c. 690-707 AD
records.description: Ex CNG, Inc. : Sale: CNG 60, Lot: 1060. Closing Date: May 22, 2002. ARAB-SASANIAN. Bukhara. Estimate $300 Sold For $300 This is the variety with the long Sogdian legend. Naymark reads: "pwx´r xr´´n xwβ xw/nn/wk" = "Bukharan Great King Khunak". ARAB-SASANIAN. Bukhara. Anonymous issues imitating Varhran V. Before 775 AD. AR Drachm (3.10 gm). Crowned and cuirassed Sasanian style bust right, with degraded Bhukaran legend which begins inside bust / Fire altar with attandents. Walker Arab-Sassanian, pg. 163, b4; Zeimal (BAI 8, 1994) pl. I, 7. Good VF, reverse die rust. Rare variety. An intermediate Bukharan imitations of Sasanian coinage, this coin is unusual in that the beginning of the legend is inside the bust, replacing the usual large pellets which represent musculature. (Lot also includes: ARAB-SASANIAN. Umayyad governors. 'Abdallah ibn Khazim. AH 62-72/681-691 AD. AR Drachm (3.06 gm). Struck AH 69 (sic)=688 AD. "Merv" mint. Sasanian style crowned bust right, pellet in annulet on chest (Gaube, brustkollier VI), title in Pahlevi; "bismillah" and crescent flanked by pellet trefoils in margin, and Hunnic countermarks in margin / Fire altar flanked by attendants; crescent flanked by two pellets in margin. Walker Arab-Sasanian 175 var. (chest ornament)., cmk. 19, cf.19, 21, and -; cf. Göbl cmk. 19, 21, 66, 109, 119; Gaube -; Album 19 (type), 92 (cmk.). Good VF, broken, five countermarks and reverse graffiti. Rare variety.) Two (2) coins in lot. ($300)

records.title: #82766 - SOGDIANA: Anonymous, ca. 700-730, AR 'mug' drachm.
records.description: Ex Stephen Album Item No. 87394 SOGDIANA: Anonymous, ca. 700-730, AR 'mug' drachm (2.88g). Bukharkhudat type crowned bust right, Sogdian legend before / attendants flanking fire altar, which is dominated by the head of Ahura Mazda, highly stylized, edge chipped. These are often called "Mug drachms" as the the first known hoard was found on Mug mountain (Tajikistan). The name was given by one of the numismatists involved in the original group, probably Zeimal, Davidovich or Smirnova. There were ancient documents found there also. It appears these coins were minted and circulated in the territories of Samarqand and Tajikistan. Through the years three hoards have been known from Tajikistan territory, one from Samarqand area and one hoard from the City of Paykend (45 km from Bukhara). These coins never circulated in Bukhara oasis however and no coins have yet been found in there even though they are derived from the Bukharkhudat types. This came from a hoard of 200 drachms. Also found in this recent hoard were 40 AR Bukharkhudat drachms, 2 Sasanian AR drachms, and 15 Sasanian drachms with countermarks.

records.title: #11614 - Bukharhudat AR drachm, with name Turghar
records.description: Published by the kind permission of Asbar Bukharhudat AR drachm. With name Turghar. A very rare, or if telling more correctly one of the most rare coins of Bukharhudat type, with a name of Sogdian governor Turghar. (Turghar is a governor which has rendered significant resistance to the Arabian invasion in Central Asia) This type of coins is published in several works of O.Smirnova and A.Belenitskiy. In their works these two authors speak on the various points of view about these coins, their origin, aura of circulation, types and classification. But, in any event, we shall try to generalize the basic sense of these works, and to give you some information, which is for certainty accessible only for few considering that these publications are rare. As known from old China and others historical written sources, the government of Turghar is exactly dated, and related to the period 738 - 750 AD. From the same sources it is visible, that the government of Turghar can be divided into two stages. The first stage, is when Turghar's father Ikhshid (Ikhshid is a title of Sogdian governors) Gurek in 731 AD asks to ratify his son as a governor of Kabudan and where he becomes a governor on behalf of the father up to the Gurek death. To the second stage of Turghar government, it is possible to relate the period after the death of Gurek in 738 AD when Turghar gets to the throne, gets the title Ikhshid and rules the Samarkand Sogd down to 750 years. Paying attention to these brief items of information from a history, and according to the bronze coins of the previous governors, it is visible, that all coins of Samarkand governors have the title Ikhshid. And version that the Sogdian governor Turghar issued drachms of Bukharhudat type with his own name when he was a governor of Kabudan during the period of 731-738 AD is more probable, as on the given coin there is only the name, but the title Ikhshid that was accepted by him in 738 is absent. O.Smirnova and A.Belenitskiy in their works agreed in one opinion, that during the period of Turghar's government the currency reform of drachms of Bukharhudat type was made. The larger anonymous Bukharhudat drahms of so-called Mugh's type were changed into drahms more small in size, but with the names of the governors. And the given coin is a confirmation of this theory. During Ikhshid Turghar (738-750 AD.) there were also issued coins on the Chinese sample (bronze with a square aperture). The first, earlier type, on metal and registration is much similar to coins of previous Sogdian governors. And more later type undergoes the certain changes. The coins become fine, and also appreciablly worsen structure of metal. Probably, the coins of late type were in use for a certain time after death of Turghar. Rarity: From the various publications, and information, which is accessible to me from quite competent sources, these coins are known a little. Namely: - 1 coin stores in a State museum Hermitage (Saint-Petersberg, Russia) - 3 coins - are known from excavation on Pendjikent town in the period of 1955-1962. in a museum of a history in Dushanbe, Tadjikistan. - 2 coins - in a museum of a history of Uzbekistan (Tashkent). From excavation on Paykend 198x, - 1 coin in a private collection. Uzbekistan. (considerably worse Status, also is not accessible to sale) - 1 coin - item #3956295889 at eBay.com. This coin has appeared in the market in 2001, and was published later. Status of a coin. Proceeding from the images in the various publications of this type of coins, our coin is one of best on safety. Obverse: Crowned bust of ruler right, circle above crown. In front of the face Sogdian legend - "Turghar", behind the head distorted pehlevi legend. Reverse: In the center of the coin altar with a head of Ahura Mazda. On both sides of the altar figures of attendants (mobeds). This coin was described in The catalogue of coins of Penjikend #15 by O.Smirnova. A.Belinitskiy. Klad serebryanyh monet iz Penjikenda. / Epigraphika of East #17, 1966.

records.description: Ex Dmitry Markov Coins & Medals, Auction 11, September 3rd, 2003; Lot 415 : CENTRAL ASIA - SOGHD - BUKHARA Abbasid coinage of Bukhara. Governor Abi Da’ud Khalid, 754-757 AD. ("Bukharahuda" type). AR Dirham. 2.98 gm. With the Arabic legend "Khalid" behind the head. Of the Greatest RARITY and one of less than 10 known. We have no record of a single piece in the West other than the one sold at our Auction Sale # 6, December 9-10, 1998, lot # 176. Slightly rough surfaces. Great original lustre. Almost EF. Abi Da’ud Khalid was one of the main officers of Abu Muslim, serving as his deputy in Khurasan and Maveranahr. He was left in charge when Abu Muslim left for Iraq in AH 137 (754-5 AD). Later the same year, after the death of Abu Muslim, Caliph Al-Mansur promoted Abi Da’ud Khalid to Governor of Khurasan. He was killed by Shi’itte rebels in AH 140 (754-5 AD). Estimate: USD 1000 / Price realized: 1075 USD

records.description: Cyrus Coins, ITEM #5187 : ARAB BUKHARAN: MUHAMMAD, AH 143-151+ (AD 761-769+), AR DRACHM (DIRHAM) NOT DATED, NO MINT, ALBUM #93, VERY RARE TYPE WITH GOVERNOR'S NAME Reign: Governor Muhammad, AH 143-151+ (AD 761-769+) Denomination: Silver (AR) drachm (muhammadi dirham) Date Struck: Not Dated Mint: No Mint (Bukhara region?) VERY RARE Obverse: Bust to right (imitating drachms of the Sasanian king Varahran V (420-438), the name of the governor citing the heir-apparent to the Abbasid caliphate by his personal name: Muhammad (RR) Reverse: similar to Sasanian reverse with a fire alter in the centre but fairly dotted crude design. Weight: 3.18 gr. Diameter: 25 mm. Reference: Album 93 Grade: good XF perfect centred strike! (ex. Jim Farr Collection ) Notes: The rise of the city of Bukhara to great prominence, in my opinion, dates from the Arab conquests and the coming of Islam to Central Asia. Other than its favorable location and its affluence, as both a rich agricultural and textile area and a trading city, Bukhara became the great focus of Islamic learning in Central Asia. Why did it become such a center rather than Samarkand, or some other city? I believe this can be answered by the circumstances of the Arab occupation of Bukhara, as contrasted with other cities, except Marv which was the first site where the Arabs were settled in the homes of the local people. During almost a century of Umayyad rule, from the 660s to 750 of our era, the whole oasis of Marv was divided by the government, which then settled the Arab tribes in various villages. The Arabs were mainly interested in raiding across the desert to the Oxus river and beyond, using Marv as a base. There was no principal city in the Marv oasis, and Marv had been a military outpost of the Sasanian empire, as it continued to be under Arabs . Quoted from Richard N. records.title: #18105 - AR, drahm, with name of al-Mahdí
records.description: Ex COINS OF CENTRAL ASIA : Bk 26. Abbasid imitation of Bukharian drachms. With name of Abbasid governor al-Mahdi. Third quarter of the 8th century. Obv.: Crowned bust of ruler right, under crown crescent with a dot. In front of the face Sogdian legend - "King of Bukhara", behind the head Arabic inscription "al-Mahdi". Rev.: In the center of the coin altar with a head of Ahura Mazda to the right. On both sides of the altar figures of attendants (mobeds). AR 25 mm. Weight 2.7 gram. /Scarce/

records.title: #16694 - AR (debased) / billon dirham ghiṭrífí, (Bukhárá - بخارا), date?
records.description: Ex Dmitry Markov Coins & Medals : > Auction 11 Auction date: September 3rd, 2003 Lot number: 421 Price realized: 150 USD Lot description: CENTRAL ASIA - SOGHD - BUKHARA No.: 421 Estimate: USD 150 "Bukharhudats". Ca. 11th-12th Cent. Dirham. 2.26 gm. Debased silver. "Black Dirham". With the Arabic legend "al Mahdi" behind the head. RARE Good VF Coins of this type, which visually seem to be bronze, despite bearing an older legend al- Mahdi are known from the hoards of the 11th and 12th centuries and are often referred to as "Black Dirhams". Different scholarly opinions attribute them to different areas of Mawarannahr or offer other explanations of their origin.

records.title: #18121 - Bill dirham, with name of al-Mahdí, variant w/ bakh bakh
records.description: Ex COINS OF CENTRAL ASIA : Bk 28. Abbasid imitation of Bukharian drachms. With name of Abbasid governor al-Mahdi. Third quarter of the 8th century - 10th century. Obv.: Crowned bust of ruler right, under crown crescent with a dot. In front of the face Sogdian legend - "King of Bukhara", behind the head Arabic inscription "al-Mahdi". Two characters instead of three dots under portrait . Rev.: In the center of the coin altar with a head of Ahura Mazda to the right. On both sides of the altar figures of attendants (mobeds). BI 24 mm, Weight 2.2 gram. /Scarce/ Remark : under a portrait is inscribed bah bah , cf. coins struck at Samarqand (# 18520 | and aš-Šáš (# 18438 ) in 281 AH.

records.title: #11520 - AR drachm, w/ names Harun (ar-Rashid) and Jaʿfar
records.description: Published by the kind permission of Asbar `Abbasid imitation of Bukharian drachm with name Harún (ar-Rašíd) AH 170-193 and Ja`far. This type of Bukharian drachm which has names of Khalífah Harún (ar-Rašíd) & Ja`far was never published and to the best of my knowledge there is no other known coins of this type which has two of these names Harún & Ja`far. Name Ja`far most probably belongs to the councilor of Harún ar-Rašíd. Ja`far Barmakí was Harún`s ar-Rašíd councilor before AH 186. Obverse: Crowned bust of ruler right. In front of the face Soghdian legend - "King of Bukhara", above & behind the head Arabic inscription " al-khalífah Harún ", below " Ja`far " and " li-Lah ". Reverse: In the center of the coin altar with a head of Ahura Mazda to the right. On both sides of the altar figures of attendants (mobeds).

records.title: #18133 - Bukhar khudat type AR, "al-Khaqan al-A´zam.
records.description: Drawing from Walker, "Arab-sasanian coins...", Nej.1 (fig 13), Nejelow Collection at Kazan. Obv: Bust right, with Arabic legend around, with the title "al-Khaqan al-A´zam". This title was used by the Turks from the 7th cent., but it was the Qarakhanids who first used it on coins. That´s why Russian numismatists attributes this coin to the Qarakhanids in the 11th-12th cent. Other opinions exists... Rev: Firealtar with attendants.

records.title: #299288 - Paikend AE cash type, Anonymous.
records.description: Ex Stephen Album Rare Coins Auc 44, 15-18 Sep 2022, lot 118. Starting price: 140 USD PAIKEND: Anonymous, ca. 640-710, AE cash (1.52g), Zeno-20199, Bukhara tamgha at top, Chinese yuan below, and Sogdian text to left & right // cross above & below the center, without the square hole in the center, superb example, VF-EF, RR. Alexandr Naymark has read the Sogdian text as PRN / KND, "city of glory", and suggested that this was a local issue under a Christian ruler, in opposition to the kings of Bukhara (see Zeno-30858 for this explanation). records.title: #50226 - South Sogd, AR hemidrachm, Phseigacharis.
records.description: AR coins of Phseigaharis (φςειγαχαρις) are probably one of the most rare among all early Soghdian coinage. Not more than 10 pieces were reported, as I can judge. Obv.: Portrait of king, with typical for Saka-YuehChi iconography. On this specimen even plume on headdress is visible. Rev.: Standing Hercules, leaning on knotty cudgel in his right arm and bearing lion-skin in his left one. Nimbus or wreath around his head. Greek legend in square script.

records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 40 14-16 Mar 2026, lot 1049. Starting price: 50 CHF LOCAL ISSUES, Sogdiana. Principality of Kesh. Wanwan or Wanun (?), 2nd-mid 3rd century. Obol (Silver, 17 mm, 0.50 g, 12 h), Seleukid type. Herakles standing right, holding club in his right hand and diadem in his left; illegible name of the king in Sogdian to left, probably 'wnwn' = 'Wanwan' or 'Wanun'. Rev. Zeus enthroned to left, holding an eagle in his right hand; traces of 'MRʾY' = 'xūβu' ('king' in Sogdian). Zeno 83144. Extremely rare and unusually well preserved. records.title: #50163 - Kesh, AE, Akhurpat, triskele in circles.
records.description: Obv.: Bust of the bearded king in winged crown of Sassanian type. Arabian legend instead of Soghdian in front of his face. Rev.: In three central circular pearl cartouche South Soghd rulers' triskeles-shaped tamgha. Arabian legend in margin. The coin seems to be struck, but on definitely cast flan. I guess, this type should be direct follower of Smirnova #1359. But Arab legend points on 8th century, thus, previous type, fully cast, with Soghdian legends and sguare cartouche on reverse should be issued not earlier than at late 7th century AD.

records.title: #202957 - SOGD, Nakhshab, AR unit, Anonymous.
records.description: Ex Stephen Album Auction 31, May 17, 2018: lot 141. Estimated At:300.00 - 400.00 USD SOGDIANA: Anonymous, ca. 2nd century BC, AR unit (1.32g), cf. Zeno-146695 for a much later example of this design, Yueh Chi style diademed bust left // forepart of a horse left, with Greek letter K to left, fine style, EF, RRR. This design was later adopted at Samarqand, and this piece seems to represent the initial style of the Samarqand "horsehead" series that would last for several centuries, rapidly disintegrating into almost childish simplified designs, as we can see on Zeno under Central Asia > Soghd > Samarqand.

records.title: #192705 - Soghd, bronze cash, ikhshid Urk Wartramuka, Samarqand, m/a
records.description: Smirnova #657 Obv: Sogdian legend MLK WRK WRTRMWK (king Urk Wartarmuka) Rev: tamgha of Samarkand (left) and the triskele tamgha of the kings dynasty (right) Compare with Z# 123439 . Metal composition of the coin is: Cu 70.36, Sn 12.83, As 1.23, Sb 0.61, Pb 14.85, Zn,Bi,Fe,Co,Ni are under detection or error limits, Sum 99.84 %, microprobe data in scanning mode on 90x20 mkm surface. The alloy is binary and composed by groundmass of composition Cu 81.97, Sn 12.85, As 1.72, Sb 0.81, Pb 2.26, Ni 0.23, Sum 99.84 % with abundant inclusions of composition Sn 6.53, Pb 93.43, Sum 99.96 % (point microprobe data). So we have here nonmagnetic Sb-As-bearing tin lead bronze.

records.title: #44173 - Sogd, arsenic low lead bronze cash, ikhshid Gurak, m/a
records.description: Ikhshid Gurak 710-737 AD, coin ca. 710-712 AD. obv: Sogdian legend MLK' 'WR 'LEK (King Gurak). rev: Dynastic tamgha to the left of the square hole, tamgha of Samarqand to the right. Smirnova #359 Compare with #1032, where obverse is turned clockwise on 90 degree. Compare also with # 37478, where obverse orientation is the same as at this specimen. records.title: #77710 - Samarqand, AE, Turgar.
records.description: Ex Stephen Album rare coins: Auction 7: Lot 95 SOGDIANA: Turghar, Ikhshid, 740-760, AE cash (2.65g), Samarkand. Smirnova-519 type II. Sogdian legend around central square hole / Tamghas around central square hole, with crescent at reverse top. The Sogdian states, although never politically united, were centered around the main city of Samarkand. Sogdiana lay north of Bactria, east of Khwarezm, and southeast of Kangju between the Oxus (Amu Darya) and the Jaxartes (Syr Darya), embracing the fertile valley of the Zarafshan (the ancient Polytimetus). Sogdian territory corresponds to the provinces of Samarkand and Bokhara in modern Uzbekistan as well as the Sughd province of modern Tajikistan. Dates of rulers reigns are still not completely certain.

records.title: #27986 - Sogdiana, bronze cash-like coin, ikshid Turgar 738-750 A.D., m/a
records.description: Close to #5464 and #16056, but almost twice more lightweight. Also some difference in obverse/reverse orientation exist. On the image #5464 inaccuracy present - side with crescent is turned on 180 degree clockwise. But on this specimen we have exactly such orientation as on image of #5464. Metal composition of the coin is: Cu 88.9227, Zn 0.5745, Sn 6.1167, Sb 0.5930, Pb 2.3025, Fe 0.4925, Ni 0.3465, As,Bi,Cd,Co all are under detection or error levels, Sum 99.3484 %, XRF data. So we have here low-tin and low-lead bronze. More local microprobe analysis gave composition in a point: Cu 93.91, Zn 0.0, Sn 4.87, Sb 0.26, Pb 0.0, Fe 0.52, Sum 99.56 % microprobe data. Compare with Z# 48603 .

records.title: #192732 - Soghd, bronze cash, principality Samitan, Nanaiabiat Samidanian, m/a
records.description: Obv: Sogdian legend around square hole nny'βy't smyδ'nč, which can be translated as 'Nanaiabiat Samidanian', Samidan being the town's name, Nanaiabiat the ruler. Rev: Tamgha each side of square hole. The identical tamghas are in the form of a semi-circle on a pedestal; small annulet in semi-circle. Ref.: Fedorov, M., & Kuznetsov, A. (2010). A Rare Sogdian Coin from the Ming Tepe Hillfort. British Institute of Persian Studies, 48, 163-165. Fedorov, M., & Kuznetsov, A. (2010). A Hoard of Early Medieval Sogdian Bronze Coins from the Ming Tepe Hillfort. The Numismatic Chronicle, 170, 446-451. Metal composition of the coin is: Cu 46.23, Sn 10.44, Pb 41.22, Fe 1.50, Zn,As,Sb,Bi,Co,Ni are under detection or error limits, Sum 99.39 %, microprobe data in scanning mode on 120x100 mkm surface. The alloy is binary and composed by groundmass of composition Cu 90.28, Sn 7.39, As 0.72, Pb 0.57, Fe 0.82, Sum 99.78 % with abundant inclusions of pure lead (point microprobe data). So we have here magnetic yellow iron-bearing high-lead tin bronze.

records.description: This is a badly effaced Chinese styled specimen of incredibly light size and weight, purchased from a dealer in Altay, Xinjiang, China. Thus classification at the moment is provisional. Personal collection item.

records.title: #107378 - Sogdiana AE cash, Kai-yuan tong-bao, rev. tamgha and Sogdian word
records.description: Unearthed in Kyrgyzstan. Coins of this type are listed at Smirnova, O. I. “Svodnyi katalog sogdiiskikh monet. Bronza” [General catalogue of Sogdian coins. Bronze]. Moscow, 1981, p.p. 101-102, 403( Table III, ##43-47); Smirnova, O. I. "Catalogue of Coins from the Settlement Penjikent", p. 177 (Table IV, #29). DH # 14.17 type. “Rev: Sogdian legend, possibly Bugh (Lord or God), which could refer to a deity, the Chinese Emperor, or the Turkish Qagan. These imitations of Kai Yuans were issued in the Sogd area (present day Uzbekistan) during the 7th century. The petty kings of the area had established diplomatic relations with the Chinese”. Compare with # # 37290 , 6283 . Unusual die axis. Samarqand tamgha (another version: Chinese key 刀 "dao" ("Knife"), stylized as a Y-shaped tamgha of Ishkhids of Sogdiana) (top) and Soghdian word "βgy" (baga) = ruler, God or Lord (bottom) on reverse. Coins with such type of Tamgha's orientation were not listed in Smirnova.

records.description: According to iconography, the coin should belong to the earliest afshin of Ustrushana, Chirdmish. But full round legend makes it quite different from the only Chirdmish coin described by Smirnova (#1419), which have only two strokes on reverse with words crδmyš MR’Y (Lord Chirdmish). Full legend, broad flan, artistic portrait and fine calligraphy could make to suspect some special purposes of this issue. Would be very interesting any attempt to reconstruct this legend.

records.title: #77713 - Ustrushana, AE,
records.description: Ex Stephen Album rare coins: Auction 7: Lot 100 SOGDIANA: Ustrushana Principality, 6-7th Century, AE unit (1.85g), Samarkand. Bust of the Afshin, slight right, wearing Persian style headress / Tamgha at center, Sogdian inscriptions around. Little is know of the various rulers of Oshrusana (Ustrushana) or their chronology as few examples have been published. The area was first conquered by Arab armies in AD 739. But it was not until Harun al-Rashid’s reign in AD 794-95 that Fazl b. Yahya Barmati led an expedition into Transoxania and received the submission of the ruling Afshin. The last uprising against Arab rule was suppressed under al-Ma’mun in AD 822.

records.description: Ex Stephen Album rare coins: Auction 7: Lot 81 SOGDIANA: Anonymous, 7-8th Century AD, AE unit (1.72g). Smirnova-1485-96. records.title: #357721 - Soghd, Fiknan, Circa 625-750 AD. Double portrait
records.description: Obverse: Pair portrait. Reverse: Sogdian inscription [MR'Y] p(n)y? nn x'tt[wnh] "Coin of Nana-Khatun (and) Ruler", around monogram of Turk runic signs "ush + uy (Fiknan tamgha?). Ref: Smirnova #1482-97; Atakhojaev and Naymark, “Coins of the Sogdian Principality of Fiknan”, type II, #5-8 On this type, the female bust is to the left instead of the right as is typical. Only 6 specimens of this type were known to Atakhojaev and Naymark at the publication of “Coins of the Sogdian Principality of Fiknan”.

records.title: #326523 - Ruler Tudun, Rev. Striking Error
records.description: Interesting specimen of the coinage of ruler Tudun (土屯王), with the reverse of the coin undergoing some sort of striking error that allowed for what seems to be an inverted concave image of the obverse to be struck instead of the tamgha. The obverse seems to also have been struck with some degree of error, resulting in a very large rim space and unordinarily small bust area. Very special specimen and is the very kind gift of a close friend. Graded by ZDGS, a Chinese numismatic grading agency with specialty in early medieval Sogdian coinage. Grading number 1121011500095. Personal collection item.

records.title: #239307 - Central Asia, Chach, King Tarnauch, AE
records.description: Ruler of Tarnavch. VII-VIII centuries. The image of a predatory animal is possibly a leopard walking to the right surrounded by a linear rim. The curving tail is raised above the back. It is possible that the predator depicted on the coin was a tribal sign of the dynasty, or a symbol of the city or inheritance. Reverse: Tamga surrounded by Sogdian legend.The rim is linear. The legend consists of two words and is applied above the inside, below the outside of the coin circle. xw b w trn b c - ruler of Tarnavch.

Reverse: Tamga surrounded by Sogdian legend.The rim is linear. The legend consists of two words and is applied above the inside, below the outside of the coin circle. xw b w trn b c - ruler of Tarnavch.

records.title: #299389 - Chach, cast bronze unit, ruler Tarnavch, m/a
records.description: Obv.: tamga in center surrounded by Sogdian legend - xwβw trnβn/č (Tarnavch ruler) Rev.: snow leopard in circular frame Dies are parallel. Metal composition of the coin (outer rim at the reverse 8:30 o'clock) is: Cu 57.40, Sn 6.82, As 1.30, Sb 0.69, Pb 33.56, Ni 0.17, Zn,Fe,Co are under detection and error limits, Sum 99.93 %, microprobe data in scaning mode on 1100x750 mkm area. Alloy is binary and consist of groundmass with composition: Cu 91.00, Sn 5.27, As 0.80, Sb 0.47, Pb 2.27, Ni 0.18, Sum 99.99 %, with abundant large diffuse inclusions of intermetallide close to Cu2Pb: Cu 34.76, Sn 9.36, As 2.52, Pb 52.73, Sum 99.37 %. We have here Sb-bearing, arsenic, low-tin, high-lead bronze. This is the most pink alloy from 4 specimens. Compare with Z# 299398 , 299479 and 300013 . According to M.M. Maksimov and M.B. Gornung these coins were cast of copper Kalmakyr Mt (belonging to Almalyk group of deposits). But tin was delivered from some another mine. In this case we can to suppose, that lead was added in the alloy not in form of pure metal, but as copper-tin byproduct of copper smelting.

records.title: #17708 - Chach, Kabarna domain, ruler Kaviradn
records.description: “Obv. Two persons in dotted circle. Sitting with crossed legs en face figure at left. Face turned to right, long hair, conical headdress. Right hand of this personage is on his waist, left hand is stretched upright in typical gesture of adoration. Figure depicted at right observed less clear. We can see here profile image of personage sitting on low throne (?) Details of face and dressing are not distinguishable. Rev. Badly preserved dynasty symbol in centre. Only three upper “sprouts” are visible only. Legend around it is executed in sogdian cursive. It begins in 10 o’clock level and contents 15 letters, first 3 and the last one didn’t find room on coin because of die displacement. Legend could be read as (k’w) yrδn kprnw xwβ – “Kaviradn, sovereign of Kabarna ”. (reading by V.A. Livshitz). D - 2,0 cm, W. - 1,6 g, Khanabadtepa.” E. Rtveladze. “Ancient and Early Medieval Coins of the Historical and Cultural Regions of Uzbekistan”. p. 249

records.title: #330564 - Chach, Pair portrait w. additional tamgha, 7-8th Ct AD, 22mm, 2.35g (broken)
records.description: Obv: Man and woman, three quarters facing, The man/ruler is depicted on the right, he has a wide cheekbone face, his hair is combed back. The ruler has a wide collar and caftan lapels. The woman is depicted on the left, she has a wide face, on her head a peculiar, high, headdress bent forward, also a hairstyle, in the form of hair raised high. In the ears there are massive circular earrings. Border of large dots. Rev: Tamga surrounded by a Sogdian legend bgy twwn g'g'n. Runic sign or second tamgha-like on the left side of the tamgha. Ref: Sh&K #177, Sogdcoins #72 The symbol to the left of the hooks tamgha is present in the photo but not mentioned in Sh&K 177. Sogdcoins.narod.ru calls it an indefinite tamgha-like sign.

records.title: #321951 - Semirech'e, AE cash, rev. 4 tamghas. Unpublished.
records.description: Personal collection item, so far an unique specimen. The excavation point of the coin is unknown as it was mixed with a hoard of dirhams from many time periods when being sold. This was the only early Medieval Semirech'e styled coinage in the mix. In my personal belief there are two main possibilities for the tamgha: one is that it is closely related to the wine-glass tamgha settlers in the 9th century, before the area's coinage was fully controlled by the Kara Khanids. Reason for this belief is that the wine-glass tamgha, when bottom part removed, becomes the current tamgha. Research by Babayarov 2019 presented at the Inner Mongolia University conference show that details are added to Turkic tamghas as local rulers seek to delineate their own rulership from that of the central khaganate or from other rulers. The similarity of this tamgha to ram horns from the Afrasiab murals is astonishing, possibly suggesting a Turkic connection. Krasnaya Rechka and Suyab are two locations that seem possible for the original casting of this coin, for the first has unearthed the wine glass tamgha coins and the latter has been the capital for the Western Turks, the Turgesh, and the Karluks, three main coin casters of Semirech'e known to cast in this style. A second possibility is that this coin's tamghas evolved from the Chinese character "元", which could be a result of Sino-Turko iconographic fusion. There is evidence that the character "元" has appeared on Turgesh coins from the Black Turgesh faction casted by ruler W'xswt'wy (recent research by numismatist Wu Zhonghua in his book "Turgesh Coinage" suggest that Turgesh coins were factionalized between Black and Yellow tribes, and that the Black tribe uses the runic tamgha while the Yellow uses the "X" tamgha). It is plausible that the character became a tamgha, though this in my personal belief is the less possible explanation. Given the effaced nature of the coin's obverse it is unclear who the issuers were. The late 9th century Arslanids have casted coinage with a reverse that has four tamghas, presented in Kamyshev 2002, and the tamghas also have possible ram horn elements. The connection is unclear, but the weight and design of both types of coinage is extremely similar.

records.title: #327084 - Turgesh, Late period cast, Closed hole
records.description: Example of a late period Turgesh AE cash with full hole, possibly because the coin itself is too thin or light to process. This might also be a recast of some local polity in the recency of the Turgesh's collapse, with very strong stylistic influences still present. Regarding the tamgha it is, IMHO, visibly not that of the same as the Otrar coins (e.g. #299540), as the latter is rhombus and has a line connection the rhombus to the arch, whereas the current specimen's tamgha is more similar to later Turgesh coins. Hard to find. Collection item of a friend and collector in China, posted with his consent.

records.title: #33693 - S#1589, Central Asia, Turgesh, cash-like coin, m/a
records.description: Thick and heavy specimen. Compare with Z# 33694 , 189825 , 189826 and 189860 . Metal composition is : Cu 89.1810, Zn 0.3187, Sn 3.7445, As 0.7834, Sb 0.9928, Pb 2.7717, Fe 0.1788, Mn 1.7085, Ni 0.3105, Cd,Co,Bi all are under detection limits, Sum 99.9899 %, XRF data. So we see As-Sb bearing, low led and low tin bronze. Manganese content may be connected with attempts of previous owner to darken the coin with using of KMnO4+CuSO4 solution. Patination is sulphide type - in some points sulphur content reach up to 3 %.

records.title: #33694 - S#1589, Central Asia, Turgesh, cash-like coin, m/a
records.description: Compare with Z# 33693 , 189825 , 189826 and 189860 . Metal composition of the coin is: Cu 55.7065, Sn 4.1952, As 2.2783, Pb 36.7685, Fe 0.8302, Ni 0.1179, Zn,Sb,Cd,Bi,Co,Mn all are under detection and error limits, Sum 99.8966%, XRF data. Metal colour and composition are strong different from #33693. Zinc and stibium absent here, lead and tin contents elevated, copper content is lower more than 1/3. Apparently alloy is heterogeneous (liquated). Patination of the coin is phosphate type (up to 2.8 % P) and presumably represented by pyromorphite Pb5[PO4]3Cl. We can suppose, that this coin was made on another mint that Z# 33693 .

records.title: #189862 - K#30 Central Asia, bronze cash, Turgesh's tamgha, runic character 'R', m/a
records.description: Kamyshev#30 Obv.: Sogdian legend around the square hole, "Fen of King of Turgesh's Kagan". Rev.: Tamgha of Turgesh and Runic letter "R" with dot in center in lower field. Compare with Z#3506. Metal composition of the coin is: Ag 1.65, Cu 89.39, Sn 5.64, As 1.01, Sb 0.85, Pb 1.11, Zn,Cd,Bi,Fe,Co,Ni all are under detection and error limits, Sum 99.65%, microprobe data in scanning mode on surface 500x300 mkm. So we have here Ag-, As- and Sb-bearing, low-tin and extremely low-lead bronze.

records.title: #339463 - Yaghlaqar clan AE, Unknown ruler.
records.description: Ex Stephen Album Rare Coins Auction 49 13-16 June 2024, lot 79. Starting price: 350 USD YAGHLAQAR CLAN: Unknown ruler, late 8th century, AE cash, type #1 (4.06g), Kamyshev-34/35, Zeno-46641, Soghdian or Uighur legends on both sides, with the Yaghlaqar tamgha on the obverse, the word left of the tamgha is possibly the name of the ruler, but remains undeciphered; this piece is of finer condition than the 9 pieces posted on Zeno and the first to be offered at auction anywhere, excellent VF. Although the Yaghlaqar clan had been in the Turfan area of Xinjiang, China, they were forced west late in the 8th century. The coins are found around Krasnaya Rechka of Kyrgyzstan, in the Chuy Valley east of Bishkek and close to the border with Kazakhstan. There are two variants, types #1 and #2, which differ only in the form of the Yaghlaqar toughra, as noted on Zeno. Price realized: 650 USD

records.title: #94905 - Imitation of type "Kaiyuan tongbao".
records.description: eBay #250762336925. "This is a Central Asian imitation of a Tang Dynasty square-holed cash with the legend Kaiyuan tongbao. This particular example is a very crude, thick bronze coin probably from the mid to late 7th or early 8th century. It is 25 mm in diameter, 5 mm thick and weighs 14.99 grams. Kamyshev shows Kaiyuan imitations in his book on Semirech’ye, but none of his examples are this thick or this heavy. Also, unlike any published Central Asian imitations I have seen, this one has the Kaiyuan tongbao legends on both sides of the coin. This is a very rare early Central Asian coin, apparently unpublished. It grades only Good-VG, but the characters are identifiable. A really neat crude square-holed coin that predates the indigenous types from Semirech’ye and surrounding areas."

records.title: #134419 - Da Li Yuan Bao from Kyrgyzstan, m/a
records.description: The coin was unearthed at Krasnorechenskoe site (Kyrgyzstan), and apparently is local imitation of such coins issued in Xinjiang in Tang times. Compare with Z##696 and 697. These coins has distinctly yellow colour metal different from one of original Xinjiang issues. Compare also with Z# 223061 . Composition of metal of the coin also is uncommon: Cu 70.28, Sn 20.01, As 1.96, Pb 7.11, Fe 0.47, Ag,Zn,Sb,Bi,Co,Ni all are below detection or error levels, Sum 99.83%, microprobe data in scanning mode on surface 250x150 mkm. So we have here yellow As-bearing high-tin, low-lead bronze very different from usual for Xinjiang issues (cf. Z## 37794 , 44241 , 158424 and 172899 ) high-lead, moderately tin pinkish bronzes. Structure of this bronze also is very unusual and enigmatic for me - it is homogeneous on back-scattered electron images being heterogeneous compositionally. Point microprobe analysa gave wide deviations of main components Cu 85.22-74.32, Sn 11.54-15.54, As 1.25-2.32, Pb 0.00-7.44. But high-tin compositions (giving elevated tin content to alloy) weren't found. Besides that alloy don't contains desseminated pure lead drops so typical for Chinese lead bronzes structure. By other words the alloy was melted under very high temperatures and had cool very fast, what implys very different casting technology. Besides that the alloy is enriched with silver. Instead of lead drops it contains small (2-15 mkm) but abundant inclusions of pure silver. They are present not in metal itself, but in products of its alteration. This means, that the bronze contains silver in concentrations below sensitivity of microprobe 0.20% (only one point analysis gave 1.57% Ag), but during oxidation of base metals silver detached from alloy, concentrated and form its own phase. So we may conclude, that such coins are local Middle Asian production, imitations of Chinese Da Li YB, were cast by original technology from local raw materials. Mineralization of the coin now (after elimination of main copper mineralization) is represented by grey films of lead (carbonates, oxychlorides) and tin (hydroromarchite) minerals.

records.title: #226081 - Da Li Yuan Bao from Kyrgyzstan, m/a
records.description: The coin was unearthed in Kyrgyzstan, and obviously is local imitation of such coins issued in Xinjiang in Tang times. Composition of the coin alloy is: Cu 85.11/86.47, Sn 11.79/11.17, As 1.03/1.49, Sb 0.39/0.32, Pb 1.25/0.00, Fe 0.25/0.22, Co 0.00/0.12, Ni 0.18/0.21, Zn is below detection level, Sum 100.00/100.00 %, microprobe data in scanning mode on 2000x1200/1200x250 mkm surface. Point analysis is Cu 88.26, Sn 9.81, As 1.09, Sb 0.34, Fe 0.15, Co 0.08, Ni 0.13, Zn and Pb are below detection level, Sum 99.86 %. So the coin was cast of homogeneous tin, low-lead, yellow, nonmagnetic bronze. Compare with Z# 134419 , 223061 and 232134 .

records.title: #172879 - Western Liao, zhou yuan tong bao
records.description: Original description by Laosa: Kai-yuan Tong-bao, strange calligraphic variety. This is a Central Asian imitation of Tang Dynasty square-holed coins with the legend ‘Kai-yuan Tong-bao’ (開元通寶). Another possible reading is 周元通寶 [Zhou-yuan tong bao]. Unearthed on the territory of Kyrgyzstan. Image source: www.amurklad.org Character 開 [kai] is written with the radical similar to 口 instead of 井 between the “doors” (門), it also resembles the character 周, but I suppose it must be a degraded character 開 [kai]. Character 元 [yuan] below the hole is written in a strange archaic script and has both ‘left and right shoulders’ (左右挑双挑元). The similar coin unearthed in the same area can be seen there: Zeno # 172880 . Also compare to Zeno ## 162023 and 162024 .

records.title: #364888 - Western Liao, zhou yuan tong bao. Rev. large dot
records.description: Listed at SARC Premier Auctions Auction 53, September18-21, 2025 WESTERN LIAO: Uncertain Ruler, ca. 12th century, AE cash (4.50g), Zeno-330709, zhou yuan tong bao imitating the Later Zhou Dynasty issue in expressive and wild calligraphy, large dot below on reverse, graded 80 by GBCA Grading Company and misattributed on the holder, VF $1,500 - 2,500 This is the second example of this rare type we have handled. See Belyaev & Sidorovich (2023) for an in-depth discussion on this series (“Apropos of the coins with the legend zhou-yuan tong-bao from the finds in Kyrgyzstan” in Revue de la Société de Numismatique Asiatique, vol. 47, pp. 37-44), as well as Zeno for an overview of published articles on Western Liao coinage (www.zeno.ru/showgallery.php?cat=9299).

records.title: #377679 - Aniepigraphic Turgesh cash (8th c. AD) with imprint of Samanid dirham (279-289 AH), found in Chach
records.description: Shinji Hirano, "A Semerich'e Hoard Allegedly from Chach" in Zeno Festschrift 20th Anniversary, 2024. https://zeno.ru/data3/Festschrift/Shinji%20Hirano%20-%20A%20Semirech'e%20coin%20hoard%20allegedly%20from%20Chach.pdf " One coin bears the imprinted in patina part of the reverse die of a silver Samanid dirham, probably due the contact with the coin in the earth, although the Samanid dirham itself was not presented in this hoard (Fig. 2, No. 70). Visible mirror part of the dirham’s field legend allows to attribute coin to Isma’il b. Ahmad (279‒295 AH). In the legend is also cited caliph al-Mutadid, which allows to narrow period of coin issue to 279‒289 AH / 892‒903 AD (see for example dirham Z‒287961). "

records.title: #329021 - Semirech'e Anepigraphic cash, Carved edge, Charm?
records.description: Very interesting anepigraphic cash from the Semirech'e with carved edge. This is the first case that I have seen personally. However, this is further evidence that these items are very likely not spindle whorls - carved edges are seen on Turgesh coins and the heavy cash coins with R-tamgha and in both cases they are rare finds found in contexts that indicate purposes as relics or charms. Coins are the primary targets for such carvings and spindle whorls are less likely IMHO. Dimensions unknown at the moment.

records.title: #326638 - Semirech'e Anepigraphic imitation, preserved original casting state
records.description: This anepigraphic imitation of Chinese cash is luckily preserved in its most primitive casting form, without any polishing or further processing. There was some debate about the function of this species, whether they are indeed of numismatic nature or used for other purposes, such as components in weaving. The craftsmanship on this specimen clearly showcases that the same casting techniques used to create cash coins was used on this specimen, drawing a link to its use as coinage. Personal collection item.

records.title: #128838 - Semirechie, AE unit
records.description: Unearthed in Kyrgyzstan. 8 rays on obverse, 8 dots on reverse, round hole. Some experts believe this is a degraded imitation of Chinese coins, some believe that it is simply a spare part (spindle) of the utensil (spinner) used for manufacturing of yarn for weaving. Funny thing is that such AE units are unearthed only in Semirech’e. Compare with Zeno ## 128831 , 47785 , 40239 , 128840 .

records.title: #332013 - AE face/tamga “sipah” (“leader of the army”)
records.description: Reverse. On the coin, the Sogdian word spδny has the same root with the ancient Iranian title “sipah”, “sipahbad” (“leader of the army”). This word is also found on ceramic items with Sogdian inscriptions discovered at Kul-Tobe, an ancient place of human habitation on the banks of the Arys River near Chimkent. This strengthens the assumption that this word meant one of the traditional titles used in pre-Islamic Ispijab (Sairam) or Nucheket (Chimkent). References: 1. Babayarov G. New Coins Of Ispijab – Sayram / Бабаяров Г. Новые монеты Исфиджаб – Сайрама // Moziydan Sado, 2022, 1/93. – С. 12-14; 2. Sims-Williams N., Grenet F. The Sogdian inscriptions of Kultobe // Shygys, No. 6. Almaty, 2006, pp. 95-111.

records.title: #305425 - Tutuks, AE
records.description: From my personal collection, I bought this around 2018 or so off of eBay. What is the correct attribution for this series of 'ash' runic square hole coins? Smirnova #1445. This type is attributed to Ferghana by Hartill in his GCC, #4.28, as well as by Michael Fedorov in his 2003 article "Money circulation in early-mediaeval Ustrushana, Farghana, and Tokharistan (6th - first half of 8th century AD)". Smirnova does not attribute it (to my limited knowledge) but she includes the findspots of Kuva, Ferghana, one from Bukhara, and three from Otrar. Smirnova also points out that this type had not been found Semirech'e. What is the reason for attributing it to Sayram here on Zeno? Is there more recent evidence that points to this? Fedorov suggests that the city of Osh in present-day Uzbekistan may be the meaning of the "Ash" or "Ush" runic letter. Is there any other evidence or theories? I wrote a thread about this coin on CoinTalk in 2019. It is mostly speculation and I did not really understand the series, nor the context for these Central Asian cash imitations, so I am sure that it is riddled with inaccuracies. At the time I was using Hartill and Smirnova's works and I landed on a conclusion of Ferghana, 627-649, by a local Göktürk ruler possibly named Kan Bagatur. This coin measures 16mm long (with sprue), 15mm wide, and 1mm thick. Obv: Runic letter "ush" right, surrounding " 'lpw y'y'n twtwy" Rev: Blank (uniface)

records.title: #368297 - Badakhshan cast AE fals, kai yuan tong bao / Arabic legend.
records.description: Ex CNG , Islamic Auction 11 23-24 Oct 2025; lot 43. Estimate: 2500 USD Umayyad Caliphate, Bronze coinage. Cast Æ Fals (20.1mm, 2.90 g). Badakhshan mint. Undated. Chinese legend kai yuan tong bao / Arabic legend muhammad rasul allah duriba bi-badakhshan. SNAT XIVc, 234; Zeno 209686. Fine. Extremely rare. Badakhshan, which is located near to Xinjiang, is the only Umayyad mint to issue Chinese-style copper coins. The obverse of this remarkable type copies a Tang dynasty cash, but the reverse has a conventional Arabic legend in Kufic script. A unique Umayyad silver dirham from Badakhshan is known dated AH 118 (Klat 157). Sold $3,000

records.title: #83560 - Khudats of Chaghaniyan, unknown ruler, countermarked.
records.description: eBay #270554323793. HUNNIC TRIBES, Hephthalites, Khudats of Chaghaniyan, unknown ruler, c. AD 580-750, countermarked AR drachm (2.75gm). The host coin is a local imitation of the coinage of the Sasanian king Khusru I. Three human-head countermarks are equally spaced in the obverse margin and a single Tokharian countermark in cursive Greek (Bactrian) script is found at 2h on the reverse. Rtveladze 45; Kuznetzov cmk 3 (reverse). Following the crushing defeat of the Hephthalites by a combined force of Byzantines and Turks in AD 565, the varoius Hephthalite principalities continued as quasi-autonomous vassal states under the Sasanians. In AD 625, the Turks took possession of the Hephthalite states, dismantling most of the vassal structure and exerting direct rule in many areas of the old Hephthalite realm. One of the exceptions to direct Turkic rule was Chaghaniyan in Northern Tokharistan which continued under it's Hephthalite royal lineage, the Chaghan Khudats, enduring until it's eventual absorbtion into the Arab Islamic empire.

records.title: #304127 - Kobadien AE drachm, Peroz type, countermarks.
records.description: Ex Leu Numismatik AG : Web Auction 24 3-6 Dec 2022, lot 1881. Starting price: 25 CHF HUNNIC TRIBES, Hephthalites. Circa 7th century. Drachm (Bronze, 29 mm, 2.53 g, 3 h), imitating an issue of the Sasanian King Peroz I (457/9-484) from Balkh, probably Termez. Draped bust of Peroz I to right, wearing mural crown with korymbos set on crescent; in outer margin, two differing tamghas and two countermarks of a lion head and a helemeted human head; in the lower part of the margin, [ιοομο ('ioomo') in Bactrian. Rev. Stylized Sasanian fire altar flankend by two attendants; in outer margin, countermarks: human head, boar's head. Göbl 289. Vondrovec Type 289. Patina stripped and with a minor hole, otherwise, about very fine. From the collection of Dr. D. Löer, formed since the 1970s. This type was perhaps issued in Termez by the Hephthalites after they were expelled from Baktria following a defeat in 561/2 by the joint forces of the Sasanian Emperor Khosrau I and the Western Turkic Khaganate. Price realized: 30 CHF

records.title: #27984 - Northern Tokharistan, Bi drachm, Peroz-imitation.
records.description: Ex CNG, Inc. : Mail Bid Sale 66: 917 HEPHTHALITES. Baktria or Sogdiana. Circa 680-720 AD. AR Drachm (2.81 gm). Imitating Sasanian king Peroz. Crowned bust right resembling Peroz; Baktrian legend and two tribal symbols in margins, countermark: head left, wearing cap / Fire altar flanked by attendants, crescent and star above; two countermarks: head facing left and combined camel/elephant head. Göbl, Hunnen 289, with c/ms 12, 72, 73; Alram -; cf. MACW 1466. VF, original hoard patina. Both Göbl and Walker in their lists of Hephthalite countermarks list c/m 12 as a reclining Baktrian camel. On the two pieces offered here, it is very clear that the symbol is composed of two animals, with the hump of the camel forming the head of an elephant.

The human head cm seems not quite clear (compare #112172 and also the other four similar coins in the category). Göbl lists cm 91 and 92 (human/animal heads), applied only on this type of Peroz-im. I guess the head cm is one or both of these.)

records.title: #289141 - Inscription of Hüis Tolgoi from Mongolia, Stone, Earliest mongolian inscription written brahmi script. AD579-AD603/604
records.description: The Inscription of Hüis Tolgoi (HT) is a monolingual inscription in a Mongolian language[1] found in Bulgan Province, Mongolia in 1975 by D. Navaan. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inscription_of_H%C3%BCis_Tolgo... Huis Tolgoi original: (This is Alexander Vovin's tentative translation.) biti-nar kagan digin sinin bodi-satva torox kagan buda kaganu ukax ukaju xiri anakay -i tin jax bodi bigiy-nar bayi dolu jaju hugbu [] biti jilonar k(a)ranyagun tuwa puror cicire pugtig nelen [] kaganu [] kato-nar dugi-d niri kagan turug kagan uc d(o)ro tayaju xiri hergin bargol palxir []haci higbij tugju ukabar-nar kagan xani julaba tunu tugnya tuwa []xa[] tu[] to[go]gun pugtigci sinin bodisatva torox kagan []l[] [] []iyu uc bitihin [] [] gux tuwa kagan torox kaganun [] pada n(i)ri kagan turug kagan []ijin ubij jalobaj darkad jaya bi []run bitig sag pag [][] j[] [] darkan ba ... ti ba ka English translation (tentative): of the inscriptions khagan and princes, new bodhisattva born khagan, buddha lord's knowledge knowing country anakay (title) promises the tribe officials stand seven times promises ...inscription stones saw tuwa ... to strike...joined ...khagan...queens and younger brothers niri khagan turk khagan reason dharma worshipped country erkin collect ... enough those who realized khagan regnal year shone that enough tuwa people...count... ... new bodhisattva born khagan of the inscription...tuwa persons being cut from the khagan who will be reborn as a khagan they followed niri khagan khagan of turks and ...directed ... free men were happy official ... wrote this inscription ... records.title: #162024 - Kai-yuan Tong-bao, strange calligraphic variety, unlisted
records.description: This is a Central Asian imitation of Tang Dynasty square-holed coins with the legend ‘Kai-yuan Tong-bao’ (開元通寶). Unearthed in Chuy (Chui) region, Kyrgyzstan. Character 開 [kai] is written in ‘running’ script. For me it resembles the character 关 (関) [guan], but it is only my guess. The top element of character 寶 [bao] resembles the radical 山 [shan] – ‘mountain’. Element 貝 [bei] of character 寶 features several separated dots (with lines between them). Probably, this is a pictographic character representing the local landscape – mountains, stones and rivers. I invented a special Chinese term for this calligraphic variety: 山冠点贝宝 – “Character ‘bao’ with radical ‘shan’ on top and dots in radical ‘bei’.” The similar coin unearthed in the same area can be seen there: Zeno # 162023 .
